title: kv-cache: adaptive memory defrag + spillover-aware eviction + scheduler integration
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: We continue to see production incidents where long-running sequences and interleaved small requests cause KV cache fragmentation which triggers spillover paging and occasional OOMs under memory pressure. This PR implements a coordinated approach: 1) an adaptive background defragmentation pass that coalesces free segments when fragmentation exceeds a tunable threshold, 2) spillover-aware eviction prioritization that prefers compactable and least-recently-used fragments while preserving hot prefixes, 3) integration hooks into the serving scheduler so defrag/evict work is scheduled during low-latency budget windows to avoid impacting tail latency, and 4) new telemetry and unit/integration tests. Changes are gated behind a feature flag and default to off for older clusters. Summary of changes: - kv_cache/allocator: add segment map and compaction routines, heuristics for when to trigger defrag (percent_frag_threshold, min_free_run) and metrics emission. - kv_cache/eviction: refactor eviction scorer to include spillover_penalty and compaction_gain estimates, introduce two-tier eviction where candidates are first considered for in-place eviction, then compact+evict if that yields less spillover I/O. - runtime/scheduler: add soft-scheduling API to register background maintenance tasks with a budgeted window; maintenance work yields if latency SLO pressure is detected. - perf: microbenchmarks for allocation/deallocation patterns (chatty small tokens, long-concat sessions) and a load test harness simulating mixed workloads. - tests: deterministic unit tests for compaction correctness, fuzz tests for concurrent alloc/free patterns, integration e2e that runs on ci/large-ram job. Backwards compatibility and rollouts: feature is controlled by the kv-cache.defrag_enabled flag and a runtime defrag_window_seconds parameter. We ship with conservative defaults (defrag disabled by default), enabled in a staged rollout for dedicated clusters after validation. Observability: new metrics kvcache.fragmentation_ratio, kvcache.defrag_runs, kvcache.compaction_bytes, kvcache.eviction_spillover_count and traces for maintenance tasks. Bench results: in our internal perf lab, the 99th-percentile tail memory usage dropped by ~18% for mixed chat+batch workloads and incidents caused by spillover were eliminated in an 8h soak test. CI: added ci/large-ram job to surface regressions. Risks and mitigations: defrag can be CPU and memory intensive if misconfigured - we add scheduler-budgeting, back-pressure signals and an opt-out rollout strategy. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] perf numbers attached - [x] feature-flag gating - [x] docs snippet in runbook
